title: Retrieval query routing: preserve exact constraints before search
summary: Route identifiers, policy questions and aggregate requests to the right evidence path without rewriting away the user's constraints.
body:
Route identifiers, policy questions and aggregate requests to the right evidence path without rewriting away the user's constraints.

Classify the request before reformulation

A question containing case ID AX-47 and an exact error string needs a literal lookup; a paraphrase of a policy may need semantic retrieval. A count of cases by week belongs to a governed query over structured data. Treat these as different jobs. Extract the requested output, exact tokens, tenant scope and time boundary first. A reformulator may add synonyms, but it cannot replace AX-47 with a more common case or turn a count into a prose summary. Candidate retrieval starts after this contract is fixed.

Keep routing observable

Record the selected path and the reason: exact ID, natural-language passage, structured aggregation, or mixed evidence. Run lexical and semantic search in parallel for mixed requests, then merge permitted candidates. A vector match can help find related language, but it cannot establish that a literal identifier was present. If a required identifier is absent from the result, reject that candidate even when its embedding score is high. A SQL query must use an approved metric definition; generated SQL is not a substitute for permission checks.

Handle ambiguous follow-ups

For ‘What changed after that?’, resolve ‘that’ from the current conversation only when a single permitted document identity is clear. Carry the resolved ID, revision and time window into the new query. If two incidents were discussed, ask which one the user means. Never copy a previous user's context or a past authorization decision into a new session. Conversation boundaries need the same rigor as document permissions.

Evaluate the router as a component

Create a labeled set with identifiers, paraphrases, mixed questions, unsupported aggregates and ambiguous follow-ups. Count wrong-route decisions separately from search misses. An exact-search route can fail because the identifier was parsed incorrectly; a semantic route can fail because its candidate pool omitted the answer. Store the original query beside the routed form so reviewers can see what changed. Include at least one question where no source is eligible and require the no-answer path.

Worked contract

def route_support_query(question: str, case_ids: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
    import re
    requested_ids = set(re.findall(r"\bAX-\d+\b", question.upper()))
    unknown_ids = requested_ids - case_ids
    if unknown_ids:
        return {"route": "no_match", "ids": sorted(unknown_ids)}
    if re.search(r"\b(count|how many|per week)\b", question.lower()):
        return {"route": "aggregate", "ids": sorted(requested_ids)}
    if requested_ids:
        return {"route": "hybrid_exact_first", "ids": sorted(requested_ids)}
    return {"route": "semantic", "ids": []}

known_cases = {"AX-47", "AX-63"}
assert route_support_query("Why did AX-47 retry?", known_cases)["route"] == "hybrid_exact_first"
assert route_support_query("Count AX-63 cases per week", known_cases)["route"] == "aggregate"
assert route_support_query("Explain AX-91", known_cases)["route"] == "no_match"

Performance and operating cost

Routing costs O(q + m) time for query length q and m extracted IDs in this small example. The expensive work is downstream: two search legs, an aggregation or a clarification turn. Log wrong-route rates by query family and cap simultaneous searches; a cheap router that silently drops an exact constraint wastes the entire answer pipeline.

Common Mistakes

  • Treating an embedding score as proof of an exact case-ID match.
  • Rewriting a user-specified date or identifier without retaining the original constraint.
  • Sending an aggregate question to passage search and inventing a count from snippets.
  • Resolving an ambiguous follow-up from a different session.

Validation drill

Build 47 labeled queries: 12 exact IDs, 12 paraphrases, 11 mixed requests, six aggregates and six ambiguous follow-ups. Report route accuracy for each family and inspect every false route before changing a threshold.

title: Document extraction: preserve passage provenance through OCR and parsing
summary: Turn source files into searchable passages while retaining the page, section, revision and extraction quality needed to verify an answer.
body:
Turn source files into searchable passages while retaining the page, section, revision and extraction quality needed to verify an answer.

Define the extracted record

A text string alone is not a source. Each passage needs document ID, immutable revision ID, page or section, span offsets when available, extraction method, language and access label. A PDF policy may contain a scanned page, two-column layout and a table whose cells change meaning when read in the wrong order. Store the source file hash and parser version so a changed extraction can be rebuilt without pretending the document itself changed. Corpus identity is the parent contract.

Separate clean text from uncertain text

Parse machine-readable text first. Route image-only pages to OCR, and mark uncertain spans rather than silently normalizing them into authoritative policy. A table value of 47 under ‘hours’ is different from 47 under ‘days’; flattening the headers can invert a support rule. Keep table headers with row text or represent the table as structured cells. Human review should focus on low-confidence pages that answer high-impact questions, not every document equally.

Retain location through cleanup

Whitespace normalization, header removal and dehyphenation can improve search. They also shift character offsets. Maintain a map from cleaned spans back to source-page coordinates or stable section IDs. When the answer cites a passage, the reader should land on the source location that actually supports the claim. If an OCR run changes, rebuild the chunk IDs and invalidate answers tied to old offsets. Citation integrity depends on this map.

Gate ingestion with concrete failures

Feed the parser a missing page, duplicate footer, rotated scan, repeated table header and an inaccessible file. Reject a document if its required metadata or access label is absent. Record page count, extracted character count, empty pages and confidence distribution. A parser yielding text is not evidence that it preserved meaning. Compare a reviewed sample of passages against the original page, especially around headings, tables and footnotes.

Worked contract

from dataclasses import dataclass
from hashlib import sha256

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ExtractedPassage:
    document_id: str
    revision_id: str
    page: int
    section: str
    text: str
    source_sha256: str

def passage_record(document_id: str, revision_id: str, page: int,
                   section: str, text: str, source_bytes: bytes) -> ExtractedPassage:
    if page < 1 or not document_id or not revision_id or not section or not text.strip():
        raise ValueError("incomplete extraction provenance")
    return ExtractedPassage(document_id, revision_id, page, section,
                            text.strip(), sha256(source_bytes).hexdigest())

source = b"Policy r8 page 4"
passage = passage_record("refund-policy", "r8", 4, "Exceptions", " 47 hours ", source)
assert passage.page == 4 and passage.text == "47 hours"
assert passage.source_sha256 == sha256(source).hexdigest()

Performance and operating cost

Extraction is O(B) in source bytes before OCR; OCR cost also depends on page count and resolution. Provenance adds small metadata per passage, while page images and offset maps add storage. Budget retries by document, not an unbounded queue. Measure empty-page rate and reviewed semantic errors separately from parser throughput.

Common Mistakes

  • Treating OCR output as exact text without a confidence or review path.
  • Dropping table headers or section titles before chunking.
  • Reusing offsets after normalization changes the text.
  • Indexing a passage when its access label or revision is missing.

Validation drill

Extract a 23-page policy with a two-column page, one rotated scan and a table. Check five answer-bearing passages against their original page and record which parser change would invalidate each citation.

title: Embedding migrations: keep query and document vectors in one space
summary: Version embedding models, dimensions and normalization rules as one index contract, then cut over only after query parity checks.
body:
Version embedding models, dimensions and normalization rules as one index contract, then cut over only after query parity checks.

Record the vector contract

An embedding is meaningful only relative to the model and preprocessing that produced it. Store model ID, revision, vector dimension, distance metric, text normalization and any title-prefix policy beside each index generation. A query vector from model B must not be compared to document vectors from model A merely because both have 768 coordinates. Even identical dimensions do not imply shared geometry. Embedding diagnostics belong before promotion.

Build a separate generation

Create a new index rather than overwriting old vectors in place. Re-embed every active, permitted document revision; index tombstones and access metadata at the same time. Reject vectors with non-finite values, wrong dimensions or an empty source span. Keep the old index available while the new one is validated. If the model changes its tokenizer or input prefix, capture that too; a silent query-side change can look like an index outage.

Compare on the same judgments

Run a frozen query set against old and candidate indexes with the same permission snapshot. Report recall at the candidate cutoff, first relevant rank, exact-ID failures and latency by query family. A higher average similarity is not evidence of better retrieval because score scales move with models. Inspect newly missed answer-bearing passages, especially minority languages and long documents. Release gates turn this comparison into a decision.

Switch and recover

Point readers to one versioned alias only after the candidate is complete and validated. Include the generation ID in result metadata and cache keys. Keep the previous alias target for a rollback window, then retire it under the corpus deletion policy. A rollback must restore matching query encoder and document index together. A mixed pair can return plausible neighbors while quietly losing relevant evidence.

Worked contract

from dataclasses import dataclass
from math import isfinite

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VectorContract:
    model_revision: str
    dimensions: int
    metric: str

def accept_vector(values: list[float], query_contract: VectorContract,
                  index_contract: VectorContract) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    if query_contract != index_contract:
        raise ValueError("query and index vector contracts differ")
    if len(values) != index_contract.dimensions or not all(map(isfinite, values)):
        raise ValueError("invalid vector")
    return tuple(values)

active = VectorContract("receipt-embed-r8", 3, "cosine")
assert accept_vector([0.2, 0.4, 0.8], active, active) == (0.2, 0.4, 0.8)
try:
    accept_vector([0.2, 0.4, 0.8], VectorContract("receipt-embed-r9", 3, "cosine"), active)
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("mixed embedding generations were accepted")

Performance and operating cost

Validating one d-dimensional vector takes O(d) time and O(d) output space here. Re-embedding N passages costs N model calls plus index construction and temporarily doubles vector storage during overlap. Migration planning should include that peak, query encoder rollout, cache invalidation and a measured rollback window.

Common Mistakes

  • Assuming equal vector dimensions imply compatible embedding spaces.
  • Replacing document vectors before deploying the matching query encoder.
  • Comparing raw similarity scores across model versions as if they shared a scale.
  • Deleting the previous generation before rollback and permission tests pass.

Validation drill

Take 83 judged queries with identifier, paraphrase and multilingual slices. Build a candidate index under a new model revision, verify dimension and access metadata, then record recall and latency deltas before moving the alias.

title: Filtered vector search: measure ANN recall inside the permitted set
summary: Approximate nearest-neighbor speed is useful only if access filters and candidate limits still surface relevant permitted passages.
body:
Approximate nearest-neighbor speed is useful only if access filters and candidate limits still surface relevant permitted passages.

Name the reference set

Approximate nearest-neighbor search trades some exact-neighbor recall for latency and memory behavior. Evaluate it against an exact search over the same eligible documents, query embedding and distance metric. If the exact baseline includes another tenant's records, its recall number is meaningless for a permission-filtered product. Apply tenant, revision and document-state filters before ranking, or use an index layout whose filtering semantics are proven. Access policy is a hard eligibility rule.

Test selective filters

A broad tenant with millions of passages and a small tenant with 47 passages may exercise different search paths. Some engines prefilter the graph; others use postfiltering or adaptive methods. Postfiltering the global top K can return zero permitted results even when a perfect permitted answer exists just outside K. Ask the engine what it actually does, then test the behavior. A filter that removes forbidden hits after they have already entered prompt assembly is too late.

Separate relevance from system recall

Measure exact top-K overlap to quantify approximation loss, then judge whether answer-bearing passages remain in the candidate pool. A candidate can differ from the exact top K yet still answer the question; conversely, excellent vector overlap can miss a literal error code. Compare by tenant size, filter selectivity, language and document length. Hybrid retrieval can recover some exact-token cases but is not a repair for access leakage.

Set a latency budget with an exit

Tune search breadth and K on a fixed judged set while measuring p50 and p95 latency. Keep a limit on vector comparisons, rerank candidates and total response time. When filtered ANN returns too few candidates, a bounded exact fallback may be reasonable for a small eligible set. Do not retry forever with a larger global K: that raises cost and can still miss the allowed island. Record when fallback runs, so an index regression is not hidden by the safety net.

Worked contract

def recall_at_k(returned_ids: list[str], exact_ids: list[str], k: int) -> float:
    if k < 1 or len(exact_ids) < k:
        raise ValueError("invalid recall cutoff")
    permitted_reference = set(exact_ids[:k])
    return len(set(returned_ids[:k]) & permitted_reference) / k

exact_permitted = ["west-r8-p4", "west-r8-p9", "west-r8-p2"]
ann_permitted = ["west-r8-p4", "west-r8-p2", "west-r8-p11"]
assert recall_at_k(ann_permitted, exact_permitted, 3) == 2 / 3

def allowed_candidates(candidates: list[dict], tenant_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    return [passage for passage in candidates if passage["tenant_id"] == tenant_id
            and passage["state"] == "active"]

assert allowed_candidates([{"tenant_id": "west", "state": "active"},
                           {"tenant_id": "east", "state": "active"}], "west") == [
                               {"tenant_id": "west", "state": "active"}]

Performance and operating cost

An exact scan costs O(Nd) distance work for N eligible d-dimensional vectors; an ANN index aims to reduce query work but adds build time, memory and tuning. The filter check shown costs O(K) over returned candidates and does not replace index-side authorization. Report recall and latency together at the production filter distribution.

Common Mistakes

  • Computing ANN recall against a reference set that includes forbidden documents.
  • Postfiltering only the global top K and calling an empty result a true no-answer.
  • Treating vector-neighbor overlap as answer-bearing passage recall.
  • Using an unbounded retry or exact fallback on a large tenant.

Validation drill

Create a large and a small tenant with overlapping language. Compare exact and ANN top-8 within each tenant, then revoke one document and prove it cannot appear in candidates, reranker inputs or citations.

title: Hybrid retrieval: fuse exact terms and semantic candidates by rank
summary: Run lexical and vector retrieval over the same permitted revision set, then fuse ranks without pretending their raw scores are comparable.
body:
Run lexical and vector retrieval over the same permitted revision set, then fuse ranks without pretending their raw scores are comparable.

Keep both candidate paths honest

A user may ask for a named status code and its meaning in different words. Keyword search protects exact strings, version tags and identifiers; dense retrieval helps with paraphrases. Each leg must apply the same tenant, document-state and revision constraints before its results reach fusion. If one leg indexes stale policy or ignores a revocation, its high rank cannot be made safe by later scoring. Filtered ANN tests the semantic leg independently.

Fuse ranks, then inspect the result

Reciprocal rank fusion awards a candidate one divided by a rank constant plus its position in each list. A passage appearing in both lists receives contributions from both. This avoids adding an unbounded keyword score to a cosine similarity on a different scale. It discards score margins, so a clear lexical winner and a weak lexical hit can be treated as neighboring ranks. Compare fusion against each leg on judged questions, particularly exact-ID queries.

Preserve identity while deduplicating

The key is a stable passage identity tied to document revision, not only display text. Two copied sections from different policies may have identical wording but different owners or effective dates. Deduplicate the same passage returned by both legs, then group near-duplicates for context selection rather than erasing provenance. Evidence packing decides how many passages from one document belong in the prompt.

Tune the window, not the formula alone

Each leg contributes only the candidates it retrieved. A fusion constant cannot recover a passage absent from both top-K lists. Measure candidate recall while changing lexical depth, vector depth and fusion constant; track p95 latency and reranker input size. If exact identifiers are mandatory, apply a hard exact-match gate before or after fusion according to the query contract, not an arbitrary score threshold on the fused rank.

Worked contract

from collections import defaultdict

def reciprocal_rank_fusion(lexical: list[str], semantic: list[str],
                           rank_constant: int = 37) -> list[str]:
    if rank_constant < 1:
        raise ValueError("rank constant must be positive")
    scores = defaultdict(float)
    for ranking in (lexical, semantic):
        for position, passage_id in enumerate(dict.fromkeys(ranking), start=1):
            scores[passage_id] += 1 / (rank_constant + position)
    return sorted(scores, key=lambda passage_id: (-scores[passage_id], passage_id))

keyword_hits = ["policy-r8-ax47", "policy-r8-refunds", "guide-r3"]
vector_hits = ["policy-r8-refunds", "policy-r8-ax47", "manual-r6"]
ranking = reciprocal_rank_fusion(keyword_hits, vector_hits)
assert ranking[:2] == ["policy-r8-ax47", "policy-r8-refunds"]
assert len(ranking) == 4

Performance and operating cost

Fusion scans L + V ranked candidates and stores at most their union, so expected O(L + V) score work and O(U) memory, followed by O(U log U) sorting. It adds almost no model cost, while running two retrieval legs may double search traffic. Bound both depths and measure whether extra recall justifies their latency.

Common Mistakes

  • Adding raw keyword and vector scores without a tested normalization rule.
  • Fusing candidates from different permission or index generations.
  • Deduplicating by text and losing document ownership or revision.
  • Tuning the fusion constant while the needed passage never enters either list.

Validation drill

Judge 63 queries split across exact identifiers, paraphrases and mixed language. Compare keyword-only, vector-only and fused recall at 12; record the extra latency and every newly missed exact-token query.

title: Reranking: spend model budget on a bounded candidate window
summary: Rerank a diverse, permitted candidate set and measure whether the added cost moves answer-bearing passages into view.
body:
Rerank a diverse, permitted candidate set and measure whether the added cost moves answer-bearing passages into view.

Find before sorting

A reranker can reorder candidates; it cannot recover an answer omitted by first-stage search. Freeze a judged set and measure candidate recall at the exact window passed to the reranker. Include identifiers, paraphrases, negative questions and long documents. If recall is weak, repair routing before paying for a bigger ranker. Hybrid retrieval can supply a stronger starting window.

Budget the input

Set a maximum candidate count, passage length and total scoring budget. A 47-passage window at 1,400 tokens each can cost more than the final answer. Truncate at sentence or section boundaries while retaining title and source identity. Test long queries and the largest eligible tenant. On timeout, fall back to first-stage order with a degraded-mode signal; do not disguise a timeout as no evidence.

Keep eligibility outside the model

Filter access, active revision and deletion state before scoring. A reranker should never see forbidden material, even if final selection would discard it. A high relevance score says nothing about truth, freshness or permission. Winning passages still need claim support checks.

Measure rank movement

Track first relevant rank, context-cutoff recall and answer support with and without reranking. Report by query family; a ranker may improve paraphrases while pushing exact IDs down. Retain candidate IDs, truncation details and model revision so regressions can be reproduced.

Worked contract

def bounded_rerank_window(candidates: list[dict], tenant_id: str,
                          limit: int = 12) -> list[dict]:
    if limit < 1:
        raise ValueError("candidate limit must be positive")
    selected, seen = [], set()
    for passage in candidates:
        if passage["tenant_id"] != tenant_id or passage["state"] != "active":
            continue
        identity = (passage["document_id"], passage["revision_id"], passage["span_id"])
        if identity not in seen:
            selected.append(passage)
            seen.add(identity)
        if len(selected) == limit:
            break
    return selected

candidate = {"tenant_id": "west", "state": "active", "document_id": "policy",
             "revision_id": "r8", "span_id": "p4"}
assert bounded_rerank_window([candidate, candidate, {**candidate, "tenant_id": "east"}],
                             "west", 2) == [candidate]

Performance and operating cost

Selecting K eligible passages from N candidates takes O(N) time and O(K) space. Pairwise reranking costs roughly one model evaluation per candidate, so compute grows with K and passage length. Cap both, measure p95, and separate first-stage recall from reranker gain.

Common Mistakes

  • Increasing the reranker window when the answer is absent from all first-stage hits.
  • Scoring a forbidden passage before access filtering.
  • Truncating away the sentence that carries the answer.
  • Calling a timeout fallback a successful rerank.

Validation drill

Use 91 judged questions. Compare first-stage and reranked first relevant rank at windows of 8, 16 and 32; record p95 latency and exact-ID regressions before choosing a window.

title: Context packing: retain independent evidence under a token cap
summary: Select passages by answer coverage, document diversity and provenance instead of filling the prompt with near-duplicates.
body:
Select passages by answer coverage, document diversity and provenance instead of filling the prompt with near-duplicates.

Reserve the evidence budget

Allocate tokens for instructions, question, response and citations before retrieved text. Each passage needs title, revision, section and citation identity. A long high-ranked section can crowd out a short exception that changes the answer. Pack by paragraphs or table rows, not a cut through a condition. Chunk boundaries determine what can be selected intact.

Prevent one revision from monopolizing context

Near-duplicate chunks often rank together. Limit repeated passages from one revision unless the question needs several clauses. Prefer a second independent source when it adds a missing fact, but do not force diversity at the cost of the sole answer-bearing span. Deduplicate the same passage identity across lexical and vector legs; copied text in separate revisions retains separate provenance.

Preserve contradictions

When permitted sources disagree, packing must not hide the newer statement just because it ranked lower. Include effective dates and revision labels so the answer can explain the conflict or abstain. Test exceptions, date boundaries and footnotes. Packet quality is whether it contains every fact needed, not its average similarity score.

Inspect the packet actually sent

Store candidate IDs, included IDs, exclusions and token counts. Compare generated claims with this exact packet, not the entire index. If support is absent, a fluent answer still fails. Claim checks decide whether to cite, revise or abstain.

Worked contract

def pack_passages(candidates: list[dict], token_budget: int,
                  per_revision_limit: int = 2) -> list[dict]:
    if token_budget < 1 or per_revision_limit < 1:
        raise ValueError("positive limits required")
    selected, spent, per_revision = [], 0, {}
    for passage in candidates:
        revision = (passage["document_id"], passage["revision_id"])
        if per_revision.get(revision, 0) >= per_revision_limit:
            continue
        if spent + passage["tokens"] > token_budget:
            continue
        selected.append(passage)
        spent += passage["tokens"]
        per_revision[revision] = per_revision.get(revision, 0) + 1
    return selected

ranked = [{"document_id": "policy", "revision_id": "r8", "tokens": 33},
          {"document_id": "policy", "revision_id": "r8", "tokens": 41},
          {"document_id": "faq", "revision_id": "r3", "tokens": 29}]
packet = pack_passages(ranked, 67, 1)
assert len(packet) == 2 and sum(p["tokens"] for p in packet) == 62

Performance and operating cost

This bounded pass costs O(K) time and O(D) counters for K candidates and D revisions. Tokenization and model context cost dominate. Greedy packing can miss a better combination; add measured coverage-aware selection only if judged queries expose that ceiling.

Common Mistakes

  • Spending the whole context window on passages and leaving no response budget.
  • Suppressing a newer contradiction because its score is lower.
  • Confusing duplicate text with duplicate source identity.
  • Citing a passage that was retrieved but not included in the final packet.

Validation drill

For 37 questions, label required facts and revisions. Pack under a 540-token evidence budget and measure how often all facts survive, especially exceptions and conflicts.

title: Claim-level citations: verify each answer against its passage
summary: Bind each factual claim to a permitted, current passage and reject citations that are merely related to the topic.
body:
Bind each factual claim to a permitted, current passage and reject citations that are merely related to the topic.

Split answers into testable claims

‘Refunds arrive in 47 hours and managers can extend the window’ contains two claims. Each needs support from the selected evidence packet. A policy-title citation is too broad when its quoted span states only the first clause. Keep claim and passage IDs together. Distinguish direct support, contradiction, insufficient evidence and facts supplied by the user. Abstention is correct when a required claim lacks support.

Check passage identity

The cited span must belong to an active permitted revision and have been included in the generator context. Resolve it to a readable page or section. A valid-looking ID for a retired revision is insufficient. Extraction provenance supplies the source location.

Test support rather than overlap

A passage about refund windows may omit the 47-hour value. ‘Up to 47 hours’ does not justify ‘always within 47 hours.’ Numbers, negation, dates and exceptions deserve explicit checks. An entailment model can triage cases, but its confidence alone does not prove support; keep a human-judged sample.

Fail clearly

Remove or qualify unsupported claims and regenerate from the same permitted packet. If the core question remains unanswered, state which part cannot be verified. Log the unsupported claim and citation ID without putting private source text in public telemetry. Count unsupported-claim rate separately from retrieval misses.

Worked contract

def validate_claim_citations(claims: list[dict], packet_ids: set[str],
                             active_ids: set[str]) -> list[str]:
    failures = []
    for claim in claims:
        cited = set(claim["citations"])
        if not cited or not cited <= packet_ids or not cited <= active_ids:
            failures.append(claim["claim_id"])
        elif claim["support"] != "supported":
            failures.append(claim["claim_id"])
    return failures

claims = [{"claim_id": "hours", "citations": ["policy-r8-p4"], "support": "supported"},
          {"claim_id": "extension", "citations": ["policy-r8-p4"], "support": "insufficient"}]
assert validate_claim_citations(claims, {"policy-r8-p4"}, {"policy-r8-p4"}) == ["extension"]

Performance and operating cost

Identity checking takes O(C + E) expected time for C claims and E citation edges, with O(C) failure output. Semantic support review is costlier and may need model calls or human adjudication. Sample high-impact claims first; do not hide unsupported claims in an average answer score.

Common Mistakes

  • Accepting a citation because its document title matches the topic.
  • Using a retired passage or one absent from the final context packet.
  • Treating ‘up to’ and ‘always’ as equivalent.
  • Reporting retrieval recall as proof of answer support.

Write 29 answers with a numeric claim, an exception and a distractor citation each. Mark support from the exact packet and count unsupported claims that survive automation.

title: Retrieval caches and conversation turns: recheck access every time
summary: Prevent cached evidence and follow-up questions from crossing tenant, principal or document-revision boundaries.
body:
Prevent cached evidence and follow-up questions from crossing tenant, principal or document-revision boundaries.

Key on authorization context

A cache entry keyed by query text alone is unsafe. Include tenant, principal or authorization scope, policy version, corpus generation, query normalization and retrieval configuration. Even then, a revoked document can invalidate an old answer before TTL expires. Revalidate cached passage IDs against current access and deletion state, or invalidate them on revocation. Document lifecycle defines the invalidation event.

Carry resolved conversation state

A follow-up like ‘What about the other case?’ needs a specific, permitted antecedent. Store document and revision IDs, not an indiscriminate replay of previous passages. Recheck access before reuse. If two antecedents fit, ask for clarification. A conversation ID is not an authorization token; shared browser sessions and role changes expose that mistake.

Separate candidate and answer caches

Cached candidates depend on index generation, access scope and search configuration. A cached final answer also depends on the prompt, model, evidence packet and answer policy. Give these caches separate lifetimes. Never serve a final answer whose citations no longer resolve, and avoid storing user secrets in a shared cache.

Prove revocation works

Test identical query text from two tenants, role change mid-session, document deletion and index swap. Each must produce only a newly permitted answer or an explicit no-answer. Log cache hit, authorization recheck and corpus generation without private text in metric labels. Index swaps need matching invalidation.

Worked contract

from hashlib import sha256

def retrieval_cache_key(tenant_id: str, principal_id: str, policy_revision: str,
                        corpus_generation: str, query: str) -> str:
    fields = (tenant_id, principal_id, policy_revision, corpus_generation,
              " ".join(query.casefold().split()))
    if any(not field for field in fields):
        raise ValueError("incomplete cache scope")
    return sha256("\x1f".join(fields).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

base = retrieval_cache_key("west", "analyst-47", "acl-r8", "index-r8", " AX-47 status ")
assert base != retrieval_cache_key("east", "analyst-47", "acl-r8", "index-r8", "AX-47 status")
assert base != retrieval_cache_key("west", "analyst-47", "acl-r9", "index-r8", "AX-47 status")

Performance and operating cost

Key construction is O(q) for query length q. Rechecking K cached passage IDs is O(K) plus authorization lookup cost. That recheck adds latency but prevents stale permissions from leaking. If it becomes expensive, use a policy-version or revocation index with a measured freshness bound.

Common Mistakes

  • Caching by query text without tenant or principal scope.
  • Assuming TTL handles emergency revocation.
  • Using previous-turn passages after the user's role changes.
  • Serving a cached answer after its citations disappear.

Validation drill

Run the same 19 questions as two principals with different access. Revoke a document after a warm cache and prove no old passage, claim or citation appears next.

  • Retrieval corpus contracts: identity, permissions and document lifecycle
  • Index freshness: publish complete revisions and remove stale chunks

title: Retrieval release gates: evaluate slices before changing an index
summary: Promote a retriever only after judged recall, support, access and latency checks pass for distinct query families.
body:
Promote a retriever only after judged recall, support, access and latency checks pass for distinct query families.

Freeze the comparison

Store query, permitted corpus snapshot, expected answer-bearing passage IDs, acceptable abstention and query family. Run current and candidate versions against the same access snapshot. Keep exact IDs, paraphrases, multilingual queries, long documents, stale revisions and no-answer cases separate. A global average can rise while one small tenant loses its only correct passage. Retrieval and answer quality remain separate measurements.

Measure decisions

For each query, measure answer-bearing candidate recall, required-fact survival in the final packet, first relevant rank and unsupported answer claims. Record p95 latency and forbidden-passage exposure; the latter must stay at zero. Some questions have no answer, so abstention matters. Compare equal cutoffs and token budgets across versions.

Set slice floors before testing

Write thresholds before seeing candidate results. A release may require no access violations, no decline in exact-ID recall and a bounded p95 increase while accepting a defined paraphrase improvement. Such thresholds are product policies, not universal constants. Inspect every newly failed query and retain it for regression work.

Canary and recover

After offline gates pass, send a small permitted traffic slice to the candidate alias and watch latency, empty-result rate and citation resolution before widening. Record encoder, extraction, corpus, filter and ranker revisions. Rollback query encoder and index alias together. Embedding migrations fail quietly when only one half is reverted.

Worked contract

def release_decision(current: dict, candidate: dict) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    failures = []
    if candidate["access_violations"] != 0:
        failures.append("access violation")
    if candidate["exact_id_recall"] < current["exact_id_recall"]:
        failures.append("exact-ID recall regression")
    if candidate["answer_support"] < current["answer_support"]:
        failures.append("answer support regression")
    if candidate["p95_ms"] > current["p95_ms"] + 47:
        failures.append("latency budget exceeded")
    return not failures, failures

baseline = {"access_violations": 0, "exact_id_recall": .94,
            "answer_support": .91, "p95_ms": 168}
candidate = {"access_violations": 0, "exact_id_recall": .95,
             "answer_support": .92, "p95_ms": 199}
assert release_decision(baseline, candidate) == (True, [])
assert release_decision(baseline, {**candidate, "access_violations": 1})[0] is False

Performance and operating cost

Evaluation of Q queries and K candidates costs at least O(QK) identity work, plus search, rerank and answer calls. Keep a small smoke set for each change and a broader judged set before promotion. The 47 ms allowance in this example is product-specific; choose a measured budget for the actual service.

Common Mistakes

  • Promoting on one average while an important tenant slice regresses.
  • Changing the judged corpus between baseline and candidate runs.
  • Reporting answer quality without candidate recall or access exposure.
  • Rolling back the index while leaving the new query encoder active.

Validation drill

Build 120 judged questions across six slices. Compare two generations at identical top-12 and 600-token packet limits, list newly failed queries and record the rollback target.

  • Filtered vector search: measure ANN recall inside the permitted set
  • Claim-level citations: verify each answer against its passage
  • RAG evaluation: separate retrieval recall from answer support

title: Project: ship a permission-aware hybrid retrieval release gate
summary: Build a small corpus, two search legs, rank fusion, evidence packing and a failing release gate with reproducible checks.
body:
Build a small corpus, two search legs, rank fusion, evidence packing and a failing release gate with reproducible checks.

Define the corpus and questions

Create 83 passages from policy revisions, case notes and help articles. Give every passage an immutable ID, tenant, document revision, state and source location. Add two tenants, one revoked passage, duplicated wording in two revisions and one table-like exception. Write 47 judged questions across exact IDs, paraphrases, mixed intent, no-answer and conflicting-revision cases. Keep judgments outside the search implementation.

Implement a transparent baseline

Start with a simple token-based lexical ranker and a precomputed semantic ranking supplied as data. Both legs must filter tenant and active state before fusion. Use rank fusion with stable passage identity; show each leg's rank and the final order for a query. Add a bounded context packet and store included IDs. This project tests retrieval logic without requiring paid model calls.

Break it deliberately

Remove an access filter from one leg and demonstrate that the test fails before a private passage reaches fusion. Swap in a stale revision and verify rejection. Make a candidate absent from both lists and show that reranking cannot recover it. Generate one unsupported numeric claim and prove citation validation catches it. Each failure should name its query and passage IDs.

Gate the release

Compare baseline and candidate on answer-bearing recall at 12, first relevant rank, forbidden exposures, packet fact coverage and p95 local query latency. Write a release decision that refuses any exposure or exact-ID regression. Package corpus manifest, judgment set, executable checks, measured output and rollback target. A screenshot of a plausible answer is not completion evidence.

Worked contract

def release_gate(rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, object]:
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("judged queries required")
    exposed = [row["query_id"] for row in rows if row["forbidden_seen"]]
    missed = [row["query_id"] for row in rows
              if row["exact_id_query"] and not row["answer_passage_found"]]
    return {"promote": not (exposed or missed), "exposed": exposed,
            "missed_exact_ids": missed}

checks = [{"query_id": "q-47", "forbidden_seen": False,
           "exact_id_query": True, "answer_passage_found": True},
          {"query_id": "q-63", "forbidden_seen": True,
           "exact_id_query": False, "answer_passage_found": True}]
assert release_gate(checks) == {"promote": False, "exposed": ["q-63"],
                                "missed_exact_ids": []}

Performance and operating cost

For Q judged rows the gate scans O(Q) time and uses O(Q) failure space. Building lexical rankings naively across N passages costs O(QN) token comparisons; production indexes avoid that scan. Keep this project small enough to inspect each failure, then scale only after the contracts are proved.

Common Mistakes

  • Treating a high fused rank as permission to show a passage.
  • Judging only answers and omitting candidate recall.
  • Testing the same queries used to hand-tune every threshold without a held-out slice.
  • Calling the project complete before deletion and rollback checks pass.

Validation drill

Deliver a repository folder with the 83-passage manifest, 47 questions, runnable gate, failure log and a one-page promotion decision. Revoke one passage after building the index and rerun all checks.

title: Retrieval design: compare lexical, semantic and reranked candidates
summary: A retrieval stage must find relevant permitted passages before generation; different query types need different matching signals.
body:
A retrieval stage must find relevant permitted passages before generation; different query types need different matching signals.

Start from query failures

A user may ask about a precise invoice code or a paraphrased policy. Exact terms favor lexical search; paraphrases may benefit from semantic similarity. Combine candidates under a fixed budget and rerank them using the actual query. Do not assume one embedding score represents answer correctness. Chunk design] changes what either retriever can find.

Filter before ranking output

Apply tenant and document permissions at retrieval time. Deduplicate overlapping chunks and cap the number of passages from one parent document. Preserve passage IDs and revisions in the ranked result. A reranker that receives forbidden text has already crossed the access boundary, even if the final response hides it.

Measure retrieval directly

Build questions with judged supporting passage IDs, including exact-code, paraphrase, multi-section and unanswerable cases. Report recall at the context budget and rank position of the first required passage. A generation failure cannot be diagnosed if retrieval evidence was never measured. Layered evaluation] separates these stages.

Control latency

Retrieve a broader candidate set cheaply, then rerank a smaller set. Measure lexical, vector and reranking time separately. A higher recall may not justify doubling p95 latency if the answer task rarely needs the added passages; decide under a stated service budget.

Implementation

def combine_candidates(lexical_hits, semantic_hits, allowed_ids, limit=12):
    if limit <= 0:
        raise ValueError("candidate limit must be positive")
    scores, passages = {}, {}
    for hits in (lexical_hits, semantic_hits):
        for rank, passage in enumerate(hits, start=1):
            if passage.chunk_id not in allowed_ids:
                continue
            scores[passage.chunk_id] = scores.get(passage.chunk_id, 0) + 1 / (60 + rank)
            passages[passage.chunk_id] = passage
    ranked_ids = sorted(scores, key=scores.__getitem__, reverse=True)
    selected, per_document = [], {}
    for chunk_id in ranked_ids:
        passage = passages[chunk_id]
        if per_document.get(passage.document_id, 0) >= 2:
            continue
        selected.append(passage)
        per_document[passage.document_id] = per_document.get(passage.document_id, 0) + 1
        if len(selected) == limit:
            break
    return selected

Performance and operating cost

Merging L lexical and S semantic hits uses O(L+S) expected hash work, then O(K log K) sorting for K unique hits. Reranking adds query-passage model cost per candidate.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not infer answer quality from vector similarity alone.
  • Do not expose forbidden text to a reranker.
  • Do not skip retrieval recall checks and blame generation for missing evidence.

title: Chunking documents: preserve section identity and answer boundaries
summary: A chunk is a retrievable unit with text, document revision and structural context; its boundaries affect both recall and evidence quality.
body:
A chunk is a retrievable unit with text, document revision and structural context; its boundaries affect both recall and evidence quality.

Split on meaning first

A policy heading and its exception should remain connected. Blind fixed-character windows may separate the rule from a qualifying sentence and cause a plausible but wrong answer. Prefer section or paragraph boundaries, then enforce a size limit. Carry heading path, document ID, revision and exact offsets. Document identity] remains attached to every chunk.

Budget overlap deliberately

Small chunks improve pinpoint retrieval but can lose context. Large chunks carry context but consume more prompt budget and may rank by unrelated words. Overlap helps at boundaries but creates near duplicates. Count distinct parent documents in the final context so four overlapping chunks do not crowd out another necessary policy.

Preserve reproducibility

Version parser, normalization, chunking parameters and embedding model together. If extraction from a PDF changes line order, a stable document revision can still produce different chunks. Store a content hash and offset or section identifier for each passage. An answer audit should resolve exactly the passage the model saw, not today’s edited page.

Test difficult structure

Create a table-like policy with a footnote, a long section and two near-identical headings. Check that the exception stays retrievable with the rule. Verify each chunk respects its input limit and can be mapped back to an exact document revision. Retrieval evaluation] will show whether the chosen boundaries help real questions.

Implementation

import hashlib
import json

def make_chunk_id(document_id, revision, section_path, text):
    identity = json.dumps([document_id, revision, section_path, text], ensure_ascii=False)
    return hashlib.sha256(identity.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:24]

chunk_record = {"chunk_id": make_chunk_id(document_id, revision, section_path, passage_text),
                "document_id": document_id, "revision": revision,
                "section": section_path, "text": passage_text}

Performance and operating cost

Parsing and splitting C characters is at least O(C); embedding every chunk adds model cost proportional to chunk count and length. Overlap raises both index size and query-context duplication.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not separate an exception from the rule it qualifies.
  • Do not lose document revision and offsets when storing chunks.
  • Do not let overlapping chunks monopolize the context.

title: RAG evaluation: separate retrieval recall from answer support
summary: A retrieval-based answer can fail because evidence was missed, misused or unavailable; evaluate each boundary with different tests.
body:
A retrieval-based answer can fail because evidence was missed, misused or unavailable; evaluate each boundary with different tests.

Build judged questions

Write questions from real user intents with allowed corpus revision, required passage IDs and expected answer or no-answer state. Include exact identifiers, paraphrases, conflicting policies and queries outside the corpus. Keep an untouched final set after tuning chunking, retrieval and prompts. Document versions] make an evaluation item reproducible.

Score retrieval first

Check whether all required evidence fits inside the selected context budget. A relevant passage at rank 40 is effectively absent when only six passages reach generation. Report recall by query type and access scope. If evidence is missing, changing answer wording will not fix the root cause. Retrieval choices] should be tested against the same judged set.

Score answers separately

When supporting passages were present, inspect factual claims against those passages, scope, no-answer behavior and conflicting-evidence handling. An answer can be fluent yet unsupported. Automated graders can prioritize review, but sample manual judgments and disagreement checks are needed for high-impact claims. Track evidence IDs and answer status in the result.

Keep an error ledger

For each failure, classify missing corpus content, permission filter, chunk boundary, rank, context truncation, generation misuse or unsupported assertion. This assigns repairs to the right stage. Re-run the same frozen questions after one change at a time; otherwise a score movement cannot be attributed.

Implementation

def retrieval_recall_at_budget(required_ids, ranked_ids, budget):
    if budget <= 0:
        raise ValueError("context budget must be positive")
    required = set(required_ids)
    if not required:
        raise ValueError("use a no-answer test for zero required passages")
    returned = set(ranked_ids[:budget])
    return len(required & returned) / len(required)

case_result = retrieval_recall_at_budget(judged_passage_ids, ranked_passage_ids, 6)

Performance and operating cost

Checking one case uses O(R+B) time for R required IDs and B returned IDs. Building high-quality judged sets costs expert review; that cost is necessary to know which stage changed.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not use answer fluency as a retrieval metric.
  • Do not count a passage beyond the context budget as retrieved evidence.
  • Do not tune on the final evaluation set repeatedly.

title: Grounded answers: require passage support and a no-answer path
summary: An answer should be tied to retrieved permitted passages, with a visible refusal when evidence is missing or conflicting.
body:
An answer should be tied to retrieved permitted passages, with a visible refusal when evidence is missing or conflicting.

Bound the answer to evidence

Pass only the user question and selected permitted passages into the answer step. Ask for claims tied to passage IDs, then verify those IDs were present in the context. A model can still write unsupported claims, so evidence IDs are an audit aid, not automatic proof. Answer evaluation] must inspect claim support separately from retrieval success.

Define an abstention rule

No passage, stale policy or conflicting versions should trigger a no-answer or escalation path. Do not fill gaps with general model memory when the product promises a handbook answer. A question can be answerable in the world yet absent from this authorized corpus. The system should say that the available material does not establish the answer.

Handle conflict explicitly

Two active policies may disagree across product regions. Preserve region, effective date and revision metadata in context; ask for missing scope if needed. Do not pick the first high-ranked text and suppress the conflict. Corpus lifecycle] should prevent retired rules from masquerading as current ones.

Test short unsupported claims

Create a question whose top chunk mentions the topic but not the requested fee, and ensure the answer abstains instead of inventing a number. Add one question requiring two sections; both passage IDs should be represented. Inspect whether the final text makes a stronger claim than the cited passages support.

Implementation

def validate_answer_evidence(answer, retrieved_chunk_ids):
    cited = set(answer["evidence_ids"])
    available = set(retrieved_chunk_ids)
    if not cited and answer["status"] == "answered":
        raise ValueError("answered without evidence")
    if not cited.issubset(available):
        raise ValueError("answer cites unavailable passage")
    if answer["status"] not in ("answered", "no-answer", "needs-scope"):
        raise ValueError("unknown answer state")
    return True

Performance and operating cost

Checking E cited IDs against K retrieved IDs is O(E+K) time and O(K) memory. Generation usually dominates latency and token cost; abstention saves unsupported downstream decisions.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not treat a cited passage ID as proof that every claim is supported.
  • Do not answer from general memory when the corpus lacks evidence.
  • Do not hide conflicting active policies.

Read next

  • RAG evaluation: separate retrieval recall from answer support
  • Retrieval design: compare lexical, semantic and reranked candidates
  • Retrieved text as untrusted data: keep instructions and tools separate

title: Retrieved text as untrusted data: keep instructions and tools separate
summary: A retrieved passage may contain instructions aimed at the model; its text must not gain authority to change tool use or access policy.
body:
A retrieved passage may contain instructions aimed at the model; its text must not gain authority to change tool use or access policy.

Name the trust levels

The user request and application instructions have different roles from handbook passages. A document can contain an imperative such as “ignore prior rules” as ordinary data, or as an attack planted by someone who edits the corpus. Do not promote that text into system instructions. Permission checks] must happen before a passage reaches any model or tool.

Restrict actions outside language

A prompt can ask a model to ignore a passage, but prompt wording alone cannot enforce authorization or tool limits. Give the answer component only read capabilities needed for its task. Validate tool arguments and destination allowlists in application code. A retrieved passage should never decide which user, tenant or document scope the server searches.

Preserve suspicious evidence safely

Log passage ID and a bounded diagnostic reason when hostile instructions are detected; avoid echoing private text into broad logs. Keep an incident fixture with a forged policy update and a request to expose another department’s handbook. The expected result is no unauthorized retrieval or action, regardless of answer fluency.

Test in stages

Run permission tests with retrieval alone, then answer tests with a hostile passage inserted, then tool-call tests under a constrained stub. A system that simply refuses every question is not useful; measure legitimate answer completion alongside attack resistance. Layered evaluation] prevents one success measure from hiding another failure.

Implementation

def validate_retrieval_request(principal, requested_scope, allowed_scopes):
    if requested_scope not in allowed_scopes.get(principal, set()):
        raise PermissionError("retrieval scope is not authorized")
    return {"principal": principal, "scope": requested_scope}

def validate_tool_action(action_name, allowed_actions):
    if action_name not in allowed_actions:
        raise PermissionError("answer component cannot perform that action")

Performance and operating cost

Authorization lookup is usually O(1) to O(log P) for P policy entries; comprehensive attack testing costs curated fixtures and review time. External tool side effects have far higher cost than a few checks.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not treat retrieved prose as trusted instructions.
  • Do not rely on a prompt to enforce authorization.
  • Do not grant write tools to a read-only answer feature.

title: Index freshness: publish complete revisions and remove stale chunks
summary: Index updates need a versioned build, deletion handling and an atomic reader switch so answers never mix policy generations.
body:
Index updates need a versioned build, deletion handling and an atomic reader switch so answers never mix policy generations.

Build a candidate generation

When the support handbook changes, parse and index the new revision under a candidate generation. Keep the current generation serving while the candidate is incomplete. Validate document counts, active revisions, permissions and representative retrieval questions, then switch the reader pointer. Backfill publication] uses the same complete-before-visible idea.

Propagate deletion

A revoked policy can remain in an embedding index, lexical index or answer cache. Track document-to-chunk lineage so removal reaches every derived store. If a deletion cannot be completed promptly, deny access to the document ID at query time while reindexing catches up. Do not rely on an old vector disappearing merely because its source file was removed.

Choose freshness guarantees

Record ingestion lag, last successful index generation and maximum acceptable age. An urgent policy correction may require a synchronous block on old content; a routine edit may tolerate a short lag. Communicate when the answer feature is stale or unavailable rather than silently serving a superseded rule. No-answer behavior] can be safer during a gap.

Drill a partial failure

Fail one document during candidate indexing. The current generation should remain visible, the candidate should not publish, and an operator should see the rejected document and reason. Then revoke a permission and confirm query-time filtering blocks the old chunk before the next full rebuild.

Implementation

def publish_index(candidate, current_pointer, required_documents):
    if (set(candidate["document_ids"]) != set(required_documents)
            or len(candidate["document_ids"]) != len(set(candidate["document_ids"]))):
        raise ValueError("index generation is incomplete")
    if candidate["failed_chunks"] or not candidate["permission_checks_passed"]:
        raise ValueError("index generation failed checks")
    previous_generation = current_pointer.read()
    if not current_pointer.compare_and_swap(previous_generation, candidate["generation_id"]):
        raise RuntimeError("index pointer changed during publish")
    return previous_generation

Performance and operating cost

A full rebuild reads O(C) corpus content and creates O(K) chunks, embeddings and index entries. A pointer switch is cheap; storing two generations temporarily increases storage and build cost.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not expose a partial candidate index.
  • Do not forget answer caches when deleting content.
  • Do not wait for full reindexing to revoke access.

title: Retrieval positives: query intent, passage identity and revision
summary: A positive query-passage pair should carry evidence for the requested answer at a known source revision, not merely share terms with the query.
body:
A positive query-passage pair should carry evidence for the requested answer at a known source revision, not merely share terms with the query.

Define the relevance judgment

A query about gateway-west rollback time may retrieve a page that mentions the service but discusses alert thresholds. That page is topically related and still not an answer-bearing positive. Record the query ID, intent, service, environment, passage ID, source revision, judged answer span and reviewer decision. A passage can be relevant for one query and irrelevant for another. Hybrid ranking can find candidates, but it cannot supply gold relevance labels by itself.

Keep source identity stable

Store the canonical passage ID separately from its current text and revision. A corrected runbook may keep the same section path while changing a numeric limit; the old positive judgment must not be reused blindly. Preserve prior judgments for audit and mark them stale until a reviewer checks the new revision. Passage revision auditing carries the source change into the index; pair labels must follow the same change.

Distinguish passage support from answer correctness

A relevant passage may require a second passage to answer a compound question. Label direct support, partial support and non-support separately. Attach exact evidence spans and policy context. Do not mark a passage positive because a generated answer sounds plausible; judge the passage before seeing the generated answer. Claim evidence contracts require the final answer to point back to support that actually exists.

Audit the training set

Sample positives by query type, source language, service and revision. Check whether protected or restricted passages entered the training export. Group repeated queries and revised passages into families before splitting. Measure disagreement on borderline judgments and how often a passage is labeled positive for one revision but not another. The negative review uses these positive labels to avoid training against a passage that also answers the question.

Implementation

def reviewed_positive_pair(query, passage, evidence_start, evidence_end):
    if query["service_id"] != passage["service_id"]:
        raise ValueError("query and passage service differ")
    if not passage["revision_id"] or not passage["passage_id"]:
        raise ValueError("source identity is required")
    if not (0 <= evidence_start < evidence_end <= len(passage["text"])):
        raise ValueError("invalid evidence span")
    return {"query_id": query["query_id"],
            "passage_id": passage["passage_id"],
            "revision_id": passage["revision_id"],
            "evidence": passage["text"][evidence_start:evidence_end]}

query = {"query_id": "rollback-47", "service_id": "gateway-west"}
passage = {"passage_id": "runbook-82", "revision_id": "r8",
           "service_id": "gateway-west", "text": "Wait 82 minutes before rollback."}
pair = reviewed_positive_pair(query, passage, 5, 15)
assert pair["evidence"] == "82 minutes"
assert pair["revision_id"] == "r8"

Performance and operating cost

Bounds and identity checks are O(1) for fixed-size metadata; copying an evidence span of s characters costs O(s) time and space. Human relevance review and passage retrieval dominate real collection cost. This function validates a reviewed span but cannot determine whether that span actually answers the query.

Common Mistakes

  • Calling a passage positive because it contains the same service name.
  • Reusing an old relevance label after a threshold changed.
  • Taking a model-generated answer as proof of passage support.
  • Training on restricted passage text without access review.

title: Retrieval prompts: pack evidence and map claims
summary: Preserve the right sections within a bounded context and check claim-level support.
body:
A retrieval context packet should carry the request, authorized passage text, document and section identifiers, version, and a declared coverage limit. A small top-k list can omit a safety precondition that sits beside the selected chunk, so the packer should fetch necessary parent context or adjacent sections before generation. Reserve room for the actual answer and review instructions; filling the entire context window with search hits can truncate the tail or bury the decisive passage. Require each procedural claim to map to a passage that actually supports it. A valid evidence ID proves membership in the packet, not that the passage establishes the asserted fact.

Operational case

Meridian's active R-8 manual contains a reset step in section 4.2 and a lockout precondition in section 4.1. The top chunk starts at 4.2, which could produce a hazardous answer if packed alone. The context assembler adds 4.1 after confirming both sections are authorized and current. The answer names the precondition before the reset, then maps each claim to the right section ID. When the technician asks for an electrical isolation value absent from R-8, the assistant says the available packet does not establish it. It does not infer a value from a different pump or a retired revision.

Packet: R8/4.1 lockout prerequisite; R8/4.2 reset sequence.
Claim A: lockout required -> R8/4.1.
Claim B: reset sequence -> R8/4.2.
Electrical isolation value: absent -> do not invent.
Coverage: site M-12, pump P-47, active R-8 only.

Performance and operating cost

Packing P passages into a token budget is O(P) bookkeeping once token counts are known; expanding adjacent sections adds retrieval and token cost. A smaller packet lowers inference latency but raises omission risk. Test both answer correctness and precondition coverage, since an answer can cite a real passage yet omit the step that makes it safe. Claim mapping is O(C+P) with an indexed passage map for C claims. Keep references to packet IDs in a private trace so a reviewer can reproduce the exact evidence shown to the model.

Common Mistakes

  • Do not clip away a required precondition to meet a token limit.
  • Do not accept a real evidence ID as proof of an unrelated claim.
  • Do not fill a missing value from a different equipment model.
